results.content: Given the inherently idiosyncratic nature of customer relationships (Grönroos 2023; Chang, Cheng and Wang, 2024), analyzing the association between satisfaction and financial performance necessitates the use of individual-level However, there is a limited body of research examining how CS relates to financial performance at the individual customer level within banking (Kamakura et al., 2002; Yu, 2007; Aurier and N’Goala, 2010; Terpstra, Kuijlen and Sijtsma, 2012; Terpstra and Verbeeten, 2014; Eriksson, Hermansson and Jonsson, 2020). Thus, this paper aims is to investigate the relationship between higher CS levels and the growth in CR at the individual level, exploring whether the effect of CS on bank CR growth exhibits a sustained effect (up to four years), and whether this effect differs among customer groups with varying levels of CS, while controlling for demographic and socio-economic factors.
